consensus_summary: Deeds performed in obedience to the Mosaic Torah, particularly when treated as a basis for justification; Paul contrasts them with faith and denies that they justify.
book_summary: Any deeds required by a law or decree, with the relevant lawgiver and duty determined by context; such deeds may constitute obedience but cannot place the lawgiver in debt or earn a benefit.
consensus_core_identification: Deeds of Mosaic-law observance that do not provide justification before God.
book_core_identification: Deeds performed under any legally imposed obligation, understood as inherently nonmeritorious toward the lawgiver.
boundary_disagreement: The book retains Mosaic-law observance as a central instance but extends the phrase to duties imposed by any law or decree, potentially including non-Mosaic and non-soteriological obligations. It also broadens the denied result from justification specifically to earning any benefit or placing any lawgiver in debt.
material_contradiction: There is no direct contradiction concerning the Pauline cases: both readings include Mosaic-law deeds and deny their justificatory merit. The material difference is that the book makes a generalized semantic and nonmerit principle where the consensus ordinarily identifies a specifically Pauline, Mosaic, and justificatory referent.
rationale: The central category—deeds done because law requires them—remains intact, so the book does not replace the consensus referent. It materially broadens that category beyond the Mosaic Torah and beyond justification, adding all legally obligated deeds and asserting that none can earn a benefit from the lawgiver. This is a substantive change in extension and conditions, making REFINED more appropriate than MATCH or DIVERGENT.
strongest_objection: The printed passages strongly support Mosaic-law observance and its inability to justify or confer the Spirit, but they do not by themselves establish that the phrase applies to every kind of law or decree, nor the broader claim that fulfilling any legal obligation can never earn any benefit. Galatians 3:10 expressly anchors the immediate usage in what is written in the book of the law.
